resolved_conflicts.explanation: The list gives 2089 with no units stated (the record converts it as feet, 636.7 m); Wikipedia gives 2,090 feet (640 m). The difference is about 3 m; the record is left as it is.

notes_for_editor: Thin. The only tower-specific source is one line on the tnlandforms list (coordinates, county, elevation, gfc-909 tag). Two searches and the Wikipedia pages found no build date, staffing, fire or fate for a tower here, and no source for the site today. The gfc-909 tag is read as the Georgia Forestry Commission number the record already holds (GFC US 909); the list itself does not say so. The record's list credit ('Tom Dunigan') does not appear in the fetched page text, so the story does not name him. The story runs about 92 words, below the guide's ~120-word floor for thin sources; hold or publish as a stub. Unverified lead: the 2013 FFLA chapter report (https://firelookout.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/cr-rp-gasc-2013.pdf) says a Georgia fire-tower status list was being compiled; no copy was located.
